rv.q: [Maureen Lipman's] funny when she needs to be, imbued with quiet pathos. She’s saluting a remarkable generation, but she’s one of a kind too.
She's a solid, stoic presence, barely moving throughout the show's lengthy run time but expressing a great depth of emotion with impressive subtlety.
There's no real resolution to this uneven work, but it's an undeniably fine performance.
Funny, heartbreaking and fierce all at once, this is a masterclass in acting.
There's real magic to this play, and it's no surprise it has seen such success.
